To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report the structure of human 5-methenyl-tetrahydrofolate-syntetase, which is the enzyme that catalyzes an important step in the one-carbon pathway of folate metabolism, and we describe the mechanism of inhibition by N10-substitutions of folate.
the structure of human 5-methenyl-tetrahydrofolate (MTHFS), an enzyme that is essential for cell proliferation and growth, has been determined for the first time.

we have determined the first structures of hMethenyltetrahdyrofolate synthetases, and have used these structures to explain the mechanism by which hMethenytetrahdyrofolates synthetases is inhibited by a series of folate analogues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis for the mechanism of catalysis and inhibition of hMETHFS.
the development of novel folate analogs that can be used as antifolates for the treatment of human cancers.
the development of new anticancer agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structures and the mutational data presented here provide a framework for the design of new inhibitors of hMTHF synthetase.
the structures reported here will serve as a basis for further structure-based drug design efforts aimed at developing novel and more potent MTHFS inhibitors.
the structural and functional studies presented here have provided a structural basis for the inhibition and regulation of hMTHF synthetase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structures and mutagenesis data presented here have provided new opportunities for rational design of hMTHF synthetase inhibitors.
we have provided a detailed structural basis for the inhibition mechanism of human 5-methenyl-tetrahydrofolate synthesis.
we have provided the first structural insights into the catalytic mechanism of hMTHPS and the molecular basis of its inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N5-iminium intermediate of hMTHF synthetase is captured and that it provides a structural basis for understanding the mechanism of inhibition by N10-substitution.
N10-substituent of folate analogues is a key determinant of the inhibition of hMETHFS.
the N5-imine intermediate is the key for the recognition of the substrate by hMTHFs.
